chapter: U Street, Jelly Roll Morton, the youth band and the WPA
title: Back in Washington: U Street and the Jungle Inn with Kay Hedgeman
summary: He goes looking for work on U Street and lands at the Jungle Inn run by Miss Lyles, accompanying singer Kay Hedgeman.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: So we came back to Washington, and I think this would be 1936, somewhere around there... When you think back, you kind of forget exactly where they are chronologically, but it's around in the same time. But chronologically, one thing might have happened before the other. But I went up on U Street. By this time I figured that I knew some of the clubs up there that I had been playing. I played the last gig down at
Fourteenth and U Street, and there were a lot of clubs on U Street then, and I just thought I'd go up and see what I could find about getting a job.

I don't know how it happened, but I went up to this... I think someone told me about this club up there, the Jungle Inn. I went up there, and there was a woman who ran the club, her name was Miss Lyles. So I went up there, and there was a couple of people working for her. There was a girl singing up there that I knew, who was very popular around here then -- her name was Kay Hedgeman. She was the one that was instrumental in me getting a job up there, playing for her. So I worked up there a while.
